overview: 38 official Qs (2008, 2017, 2019, 2025). The 73rd Amendment dominates (17), then the 74th (7) and the Community Development Programme (6); Balwant Rai Mehta and Ashok Mehta give 5, centralisation/decentralisation 3. Questions ask numbers (29/18 items, 16 Articles, tiers, term), dates (1952, 1957, 24 April / 1 June 1993), which Schedule holds an item, and where Part IX does not apply; 2025 added statement-based, chronology and assertion-reason.

possibility.angle: Centralisation vs decentralisation (Ripon, direct democracy, revitalisation committees)
possibility.what_they_ask: Father of local self-government (Lord Ripon 1882); Gram Sabha as direct democracy; L.M. Singhvi chaired the 1986 revitalisation committee.
start date (2 Oct 1952); Grow More Food Enquiry (V.T. Krishnamachari); aim of people's participation; extension principles and training methods (applied science and democratic approach, role play).
report year 1957; three-tier 'democratic decentralisation'; place in chronology of PR committees.
two-tier (Zilla Parishad, Mandal Panchayat) with four-year term; appointed by Janata govt under Morarji Desai (1977).

Eleventh Schedule 29 items and which subjects; 16 Articles (243–243O); three-tier; Gram Sabha = registered voters; exempted States (Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram); Art 243D reservation (BC optional); election within 6 months; age 21; SEC and SFC roles; AP Panchayat Secretary functions.

Part IXA; Twelfth Schedule 18 items and which subjects (cattle pounds, slaughter houses, burial grounds); in force 1 June 1993; first municipal corporation (Madras 1688); functionaries (Mayor, Chairperson, Councillor); AP municipal count (time-sensitive).

traps.trap: Swaps the item counts of the two Schedules [29 vs 18]
traps.spot: A number beside 'Eleventh' or 'Twelfth' Schedule, or '18 functional items for panchayats'
traps.fix: Eleventh (panchayats, Art 243G) = 29; Twelfth (municipalities, Art 243W) = 18. Higher number = rural, which has more subjects.
traps.pyq: Eleventh Schedule → 29 [group2-2008-paper2#130]; '18 functional items placed within panchayats' → not correct [mains-2025-paper1#118]

traps.trap: Moves a municipal subject into the Eleventh Schedule (or the reverse)
traps.spot: 'As per the Eleventh / Twelfth Schedule' with mixed items
traps.fix: Urban-only items (slaughter houses, land-use regulation, burial grounds, cattle pounds) are Twelfth; libraries, non-conventional energy, small-scale industries, technical and vocational education are Eleventh.

traps.trap: Swaps tiers between the committees and the Act
traps.spot: Options '2 / 3 tier' with a committee or 'feature of the 73rd Amendment'
traps.fix: Balwant Rai Mehta – three-tier; Ashok Mehta – two-tier, 4-year term; 73rd Amendment – three-tier (intermediate optional below 20 lakh).
traps.pyq: 'Two-tier System' → not a feature of the 73rd Amd [group2-2008-paper2#129]; Ashok Mehta → two tier with four-year term [mains-2025-paper1#134]

traps.trap: Changes the time limit for fresh elections
traps.fix: Art 243E(3): elections before expiry of 5 years or within 6 months of dissolution.
traps.pyq: 'Within 3 months' → incorrect, so i, iii and iv only [mains-2025-paper1#136]

traps.trap: Turns a voluntary provision into a compulsory one
traps.spot: Lists of 73rd Amd provisions including BC reservation
traps.fix: Compulsory: Gram Sabha, three tiers, direct election, SC/ST and one-third women reservation, SEC, SFC. Voluntary: BC reservation (243D(6)), powers and functions devolution, MLA/MP representation.
traps.pyq: 'Reservation of seats for BCs is compulsory' → not correct [mains-2025-paper1#118]

traps.trap: Mixes the commencement dates of the 73rd and 74th
traps.spot: Options 24 April and 1 June across 1992 and 1993
traps.fix: Both passed 1992; 73rd in force 24 April 1993 (Panchayati Raj Day), 74th in force 1 June 1993.

traps.trap: Defines the Gram Sabha by age or residence instead of the electoral roll
traps.fix: Art 243(b): persons registered in the electoral rolls of the village.
traps.pyq: Members of Gram Sabha → all voters as per electoral rolls [prelims-2017#62]

traps.trap: Includes an exempted State under Part IX
traps.fix: Art 243M: not applicable to Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram (and scheduled/hill areas); J&K was outside until 2019.
traps.pyq: 73rd Amd applies to → Orissa [group2-2008-paper2#133]; not applicable (2017) → Mizoram, Nagaland and J&K [mains-2017-paper1#102]

techniques.name: Rural vs urban sort [Eleventh / Twelfth]
techniques.how: Ask whether the subject only makes sense in a town (land-use regulation, slaughter houses, burial grounds, cattle pounds, urban planning) → Twelfth; farm, village industry, rural welfare → Eleventh.
techniques.example: Non-conventional energy, small-scale industries, vocational education are village development items → fall; cattle pounds is a municipal civic item → Cattle Pounds [mains-2025-paper1#143]

techniques.name: PR committee timeline
techniques.how: Line them up: Grow More Food (1952) → CDP 1952 → Balwant Rai Mehta 1957 → Ashok Mehta 1977–78 / Dantwala 1978 → G.V.K. Rao 1985 → L.M. Singhvi 1986 → Gadgil 1988 → 73rd/74th 1992. Fix the first and last, then the middle.
techniques.example: Balwant Rai Mehta (1957) first, Gadgil (1988) last → only 'd, b, c, a' keeps Dantwala 1978 before Singhvi 1986 [mains-2025-paper1#90]

techniques.name: Article-number check inside Part IX
techniques.how: Recall the key 243 letters: 243 definitions, 243A Gram Sabha, 243B tiers, 243D reservation, 243E duration, 243F disqualification (age 21), 243G Eleventh Schedule, 243-I SFC, 243K SEC, 243M exemptions.
techniques.example: Reservation of SC/ST seats in PRIs → 243D [mains-2019-paper2#126]

techniques.name: Assertion-reason: status shift test
techniques.how: If R says the Act moved PRIs from DPSP (Art 40, non-justiciable) into enforceable constitutional provisions, that is the cause of the 'landmark' – R explains A.
techniques.example: 73rd Amd is a landmark because it brought PRIs under the justiciable part → R explains A [mains-2025-paper1#110]

techniques.name: Who-runs-what elimination
techniques.how: Separate bodies: SEC – panchayat and municipal elections; ECI – Parliament, State legislatures, President, VP; SFC – local finances. Eliminate options belonging to another body.
techniques.example: State Legislatures go to ECI, co-operatives to their own authority → SEC conducts elections to Local Bodies [mains-2025-paper1#89]

confusions.remember: Balwant – three tiers, democratic decentralisation; Ashok – two tiers, four-year term, party participation.
73rd in force (Panchayati Raj Day) vs 74th in force.
Sabha = all registered voters (direct democracy); Panchayat = elected body headed by the Sarpanch.
SEC conducts local elections; SFC reviews local finances every 5 years.
Sarpanch – village panchayat; Chairperson – municipality; Mayor – corporation; Councillor – ward.
Singhvi – revitalisation of PRIs, constitutional status; G.V.K. Rao – administrative arrangements for rural development.
Dantwala – block-level planning; Gadgil – policy committee before the 1989 Bill.
CDP launched 2 Oct 1952; NES followed in 1953.
Ripon's 1882 resolution – 'Father of Local Self-Government'; Mayo's 1870 resolution on financial decentralisation.
Madras is India's first municipal corporation.

anchors: CDP 2 Oct 1952; Grow More Food Enquiry – V.T. Krishnamachari
Balwant Rai Mehta report 1957 – three tiers
Ashok Mehta 1977–78 – two tiers, four-year term (Morarji Desai govt)
73rd Amd: Part IX, 16 Articles (243–243O), Eleventh Schedule 29 items, in force 24 April 1993
74th Amd: Part IXA, Twelfth Schedule 18 items, in force 1 June 1993
Art 243D – SC/ST and one-third women reservation; BC optional
Art 243E – 5-year term, elections within 6 months of dissolution
checklist: Eleventh or Twelfth? Rural item → 29-item list; urban civic item → 18-item list.
Which committee: three tiers (Balwant) or two (Ashok)?
Compulsory or voluntary provision of the 73rd Amd?
Dates: passing year 1992 vs commencement 1993 (24 April / 1 June).
Numbers in statements: 6 months, age 21, one-third, 5 years – check each.
Chronology: fix first and last committee, then the middle.
